worked_examples.title: Customer onboarding portal — payments firm
worked_examples.content_md:
# Customer Onboarding Portal — Business Requirements Document

## 1. Context

Our existing customer-onboarding flow takes 9 working days end-to-end. Competitors are quoting 48 hours. The new portal needs to compress the manual KYC steps to under 24 hours of total wall-clock time without compromising regulatory standing.

## 2. Scope

### In scope
- New customer KYC capture flow (UK + US)
- Document upload + auto-classification
- Status dashboard for the customer success team
- Audit log of every state transition

### Out of scope
- Existing customer re-verification (Phase 2)
- Mobile native app (web-only at launch)
- Onboarding for corporate customers (separate stream)

## 3. Stakeholders

| Name | Role | Decision rights | Influence |
|------|------|-----------------|-----------|
| Priya Rao | Customer Success Director | Yes — scope owner | High |
| Sam Palmer | Engineering Lead | Yes — feasibility owner | High |
| Marcus Klein | Compliance Lead | Veto rights on KYC flow | High |
| Lin Chen | Design Lead | No — consult | Medium |

## 4. Regulatory context

FCA SUP 11 (customer due diligence), GDPR Art. 6 + Art. 9, ICO age-of-consent guidance. Audit evidence required for every KYC decision; retention 7 years.

## 5. Functional requirements

1. New customers can submit identity documents via a mobile-web flow that meets WCAG 2.2 AA.
2. Documents are auto-classified (passport / driving licence / utility bill / other) with confidence scores; below-threshold classifications route to manual review.
3. The customer can see their submission status in plain language — never a status code.
4. Compliance staff can flag a submission for additional checks without breaking the customer-facing timeline.
5. Every state transition is recorded with timestamp + actor + reason.

## 6. Non-functional requirements

- Performance: P95 page load < 2.5s on mid-tier mobile devices over UK 4G.
- Security: Documents encrypted at rest using AES-256; transit TLS 1.3; document URLs single-use, 24h TTL.
- Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA. Keyboard-navigable.
- Data residency: UK customer data in eu-west-2; US in us-east-1. No cross-border replication.

## 7. Constraints and assumptions

- Build on existing identity service (no new auth stack).
- We assume the document-classifier vendor's accuracy claim of 94% holds; if it falls below 90% in production we add a manual triage step.

## 8. Audit trail

State-transition log retained 7 years. Each entry: timestamp, actor (customer or staff ID), state before, state after, reason. Exportable to CSV on demand for FCA review.

## 9. Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Document classifier accuracy degrades under adversarial submissions | Delayed approvals; customer complaints | Manual triage fallback + monthly accuracy audit |
| Customer success team can't keep up with manual-review queue at launch volume | Onboarding bottleneck reverts to 9-day baseline | Pre-launch capacity model + auto-escalation when queue > 4h |

## 10. Sign-off

_Priya Rao + Marcus Klein + Sam Palmer; date to follow at hand-off._

annotations.note: Context paragraphs that lead with a number — "9 days vs 48 hours" — get read. Vague "we want to modernise the customer experience" intros do not.
Explicit out-of-scope items save you three meetings each. Always list them.
This is the section everyone skips. Don't. Cite the regulation by section number; engineers cannot push back on a number.
Audit trail spec at BRD time is what stops compliance from rewriting the doc post-hoc.

common_mistakes: Stakeholder table without decision rights — leaves the document unable to settle disputes.
Requirements written as solutions ("the system must use OAuth") instead of capabilities ("the customer must authenticate without remembering a separate password").
Missing the regulatory-context section because nobody asked for it. Six months in, when an audit lands, this is the section that should have existed.
Audit-trail spec deferred to engineering — engineering builds what's specified; if you don't spec what to log, they log what's convenient.
variant_patterns: Standard variant: drop §4 Regulatory Context, drop §8 Audit Trail, fold security under non-functional. Keep the rest.
Greenfield variant: add §1.5 "Why now" and §2.3 "Alternatives considered" to anchor the build-vs-buy conversation that almost always derails greenfield work.
